positions.name: ABM Industries Incorporated
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 9/11 (Friday) or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 EARNINGS BEAT + GUIDANCE RAISE + NEW 52-WEEK HIGH + 2.83x VOLUME - THE CLEANEST SETUP IN THE BOOK: ABM reported FQ3 before the 9/8 open with adjusted EPS of $1.04 vs the $1.01 consensus (+27% year over year) on revenue of $2.317B vs $2.310B expected, then RAISED the midpoint of FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $3.95-$4.10 (from $3.85-$4.15) and lifted the full-year free-cash-flow outlook to $210M from $185M. It also hit its sub-3x leverage target a full quarter early at 2.9x. The stock rose 7.6% to close at 50.60 against a 50.93 session high that IS a new 52-week high, on 1.00M shares versus a 354K 30-day average - 2.83x relative volume, by far the heaviest participation of anything I priced today, and it did this on a session where the Dow fell 1.2%. The strategic story is real: semiconductor revenue grew 65% organically, the microgrid business has quadrupled since 2022, and management said on the call the data-center pipeline is now 'a multiple of where it stood a year ago'. Those three businesses are ~$775M of nine-month revenue, 11% of the total, at double-digit blended operating margin.
positions.risks: THE HEADLINE BEAT WAS THREE CENTS AND REVENUE ONLY MATCHED THE STREET - the 7.6% move is a re-rating on the data-center narrative rather than on the quarter itself, and narrative-driven re-ratings give back quickly. Technical Solutions revenue came in BELOW the company's own expectations on roughly $15M of client project deferrals, and the Q4 guide leans heavily on those deferred projects landing on time; if they slip again the FY guide is at risk. Business & Industry revenue fell 2.6% and management does not expect it to return to organic growth until the middle of fiscal 2027, with Northern California explicitly called out as still deteriorating. Aviation margin fell year over year to 5.6% from 6.8% because airline customers are demanding cost relief on higher jet fuel - and with WTI at $93.71 that pressure gets worse, not better, which is an under-appreciated link between this position and the energy theme that dominates the rest of this book. At a $2.97B market cap on 354K average shares this is also the least liquid non-tanker name here, and I am buying at a 52-week high with no overhead support. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.
positions.driver: Tier 1: FQ3 beat, raised FY26 EPS and FCF guidance, new 52-week high on 2.8x volume

positions.name: Valero Energy Corporation
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 9/11 (Friday) or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 CRACK-SPREAD BREAKOUT TO A NEW 52-WEEK HIGH ON A NAMED SUPPLY SHOCK: on 9/8 Yemen's Iran-allied Houthi group struck Saudi Aramco facilities across Abha, Najran and Jazan, injuring 73 people per the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and US Central Command confirmed it had struck three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday after Tehran fired ballistic missiles at two US Navy warships. WTI rose 2.4% to $93.71 and Brent 1.9% to $98.79. Valero closed at 382.85 and its 384.26 intraday high IS a new 52-week high set today, on 2.74M shares versus a 2.46M 30-day average. The critical distinction versus the rest of the energy complex: refiners were the ONLY energy sub-group that closed at their highs. Every integrated and E&P I priced - XOM, CVX, COP, EOG, FANG, APA, OXY - spiked intraday and then closed at or near its session LOW as crude gave back its intraday peak of $94.73. Attacks on Saudi refining and export infrastructure threaten refined-product supply faster than crude availability, which widens crack spreads, and the tape voted for that thesis specifically. 15.4x earnings.
positions.risks: I AM RE-ENTERING A NAME THIS BOOK JUST CLOSED FOR A +6.3% GAIN, WHICH MEANS I AM PAYING 22.69 POINTS MORE THAN THE PREVIOUS ENTRY FOR THE SAME THESIS. Buying at a 52-week high on day one of a headline leaves no cushion whatsoever: a de-escalation or ceasefire signal takes the crack-spread premium out overnight and no stop protects against a gap. Crude is Valero's raw material, so sustained $93 WTI is a genuine cost increase that only helps if product cracks widen faster than feedstock - a second-order spread bet, not a direct read on the headline. Volume of 1.11x average is real but unremarkable. VLO has run from 153.20 on 9/5/2025 to 384.26 today, a 151% move in twelve months, so the great majority of this re-rating is behind us and I am buying the last leg. This is also one of four Energy Minerals names, and combined with three tanker positions this book has seven of eleven names levered to one Middle East variable. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.
positions.driver: Tier 1: Houthi strikes on Saudi Aramco, refiner breakout to a new 52-week high

MPC goes ex-dividend 8/19 (already passed) but pays 9/10, inside no relevant window. It has run from 161.93 on 12/31/2025 to 399.58, a 147% twelve-month move. Correlated with VLO, PSX and DINO to the point that these four are effectively one crack-spread position expressed four ways. Overnight only.

positions.name: Frontline plc
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 9/11 (Friday) or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 THE PUREST EXPRESSION OF THE ACTUAL EVENT - TANKERS WERE PHYSICALLY ATTACKED: US Central Command confirmed it struck three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday in response to Tehran firing ballistic missiles at two US Navy warships, and on 9/8 the Houthis struck Saudi Aramco facilities at Abha, Najran and Jazan. When tankers are the target rather than a bystander, war-risk insurance premia and rerouting away from Hormuz drive ton-mile demand and spot rates directly - this is a revenue event for tanker owners, not a sentiment spillover. Frontline closed 46.62 with a 47.215 high that IS a new 52-week high set 9/8, on 2.34M shares versus a 2.27M 30-day average (1.03x). It trades at 6.9x earnings with a 6.79% dividend yield and a $10.4B market cap, the largest of the pure tanker owners. Cheap, paid to wait, and levered to the one variable actually in the headlines.
positions.risks: TANKER EQUITIES ARE THE MOST VIOLENTLY MEAN-REVERTING GROUP IN THE MARKET - spot rates can halve in a fortnight and the equities front-run both directions, so a 6.9x multiple is a mid-cycle illusion rather than a valuation floor. FRO has run from 20.47 on 1/2/2026 to 47.215, a 131% move in eight months, and I am buying at the very top of that. It goes EX-DIVIDEND ON 9/18 for $2.61 - outside my 9/11 exit window, so I collect nothing and simply carry the risk that holders position around it. Frontline is Cyprus-domiciled with a concentrated controlling shareholder and its fleet is heavily VLCC-weighted, which is the segment most exposed if Hormuz traffic actually stops rather than merely reprices. A negotiated de-escalation is the single scenario that hurts this position most and it is entirely plausible. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.
positions.driver: Tier 1: CENTCOM strikes on three Iranian tankers, war-risk rate spike, new 52-week high

positions.name: Roivant Sciences Ltd.
positions.exitRule: Overnight (next-day open) - flat on the 9/9 open
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 POSITIVE PHASE 2 CLINICAL DATA - THE ONLY CATALYST IN THIS BOOK WITH NO CONNECTION WHATSOEVER TO OIL: Roivant released topline data from its Phase 2 PHocus trial of mosliciguat in pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) on 9/8. The stock rose roughly 17% to close at 41.48 against a 42.50 intraday high that IS a new 52-week high, on 24.67M shares versus a 7.51M 30-day average - 3.28x relative volume, the highest of any position in this book. It closed in the upper half of its 38.41-42.50 range rather than fading, which separates it from Pharvaris, which released positive Phase 3 HAE data the same day, spiked to 43.25 and then collapsed to close at 37.84 near its session low - I priced PHVS and rejected it for exactly that reason. At a $29.96B market cap ROIV is a genuine large-cap, and it is the single most valuable diversifier available today given healthcare was the worst-performing sector (-2%) on a session energy led.
positions.risks: ROIVANT HAS NO EARNINGS - THE TRAILING P/E IS -79.6 AND THIS IS A 6.0x-BOOK PRE-PROFIT BIOTECH, so there is no valuation anchor of any kind. More importantly this is Phase 2 data, not Phase 3: PH-ILD is a graveyard indication where multiple programmes have produced encouraging mid-stage results and then failed to confirm, and a 17% one-day move on Phase 2 topline is the market pricing an outcome that is still years and one large trial from approval. Buying the day after a 17% clinical pop is chasing by definition, and clinical pops routinely give back a third to a half of the move within a week as event-driven holders exit into the liquidity. It also closed at 41.48 versus the 42.50 high, so the fade had already begun into the bell. The 3.28x volume that I am citing as confirmation is equally consistent with a full rotation of the shareholder base from long-term holders to fast money. I am taking the gap and leaving - overnight only, no day-2 exposure.
positions.driver: Tier 1: positive Phase 2 PHocus topline data, new 52-week high on 3.3x volume

A single 2.5% day in copper is a thin reed - if it was short-covering rather than physical demand it reverses immediately. Overnight only.
